issues: All three quotes were re-fetched fresh (cache cleared) and are verbatim on their pages. The dates hold: DOF publication on 5 July 2010, and a replacement law of the same name published on 20 March 2025.

Off-by-one precision: the note says the law 'was abrogated' on 20 March 2025. The 2025 decree was published that day, but its first transitional article puts it in force the day after publication, and its second says the 2010 law is abrogated 'a la entrada en vigor del presente Decreto', which is 21 March 2025. The note now says the decree was published on 20 March and took effect the next day.

Three claims in the note had no source: IFAI supervision, the 2017 public-sector general law and the dissolution of the INAI. The DLA Piper quotes only say that the Ministry is now the data authority. Primary texts from the Cámara de Diputados were added. They are the 2010 DOF original (IFAI defined as 'Instituto'; Art. 38 supervision; in force the next day), the 2025 decree (its abrogation list names the 2010 law and the 2017 Ley General de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de Sujetos Obligados; 'Secretaría' is defined as the Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno), and the 20 December 2024 constitutional decree on 'simplificación orgánica', which extinguishes the bodies it covers, the INAI among them.

DLA Piper's own page has an error that is not quoted in the record. It says the 2010 law 'was in force until July 6, 2010', when that is the day it entered into force. The quotes used in the record are unaffected.

fieldFixes.note: Private-sector law published in the Diario Oficial on 5 July 2010 and in force the next day, supervised by the IFAI (later INAI); a separate general law for the public sector followed in 2017. A decree published on 20 March 2025 and in force the next day abrogated both and replaced the 2010 law with a new federal law of the same name; the INAI was dissolved and the Ministry of Anticorruption and Good Governance (Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno) became the data authority.

issues: The note is incomplete. It gives only the 6 January 2012 proclamation, but the official Digital Legislative Library (laws.gov.tt) lists a second one. Legal Notice 220 of 2021, a proclamation dated 20 August 2021, brought section 42(a) and (b) of Part III into operation on 23 August 2021. That section covers disclosure of personal information by public bodies.

DLA Piper's second quote is verbatim, but it runs the two proclamations together. It lists '42(a),(b) of Part III' in the same sentence as 'partially enacted on January 6, 2012 by Legal Notice 2 of 2012'. Legal Notice 2 of 2012 itself names only Part I and sections 7 to 18, 22, 23, 25(1), 26 and 28 of Part II. DLA also says 'enacted' where the event was a proclamation, and the page notes it was 'last reviewed in 2023'. Source index 1 is repointed to the primary Legal Notice 2 of 2012.

The Act was assented to on 22 June 2011 (Act No. 13 of 2011), so yearEnacted 2011 is correct. The official database still marks the Act 'only … partially proclaimed'. Part IV (private sector) and Part V (enforcement) are not among the proclaimed provisions, so the claim 'only partly proclaimed' stands.

fieldFixes.note: Assented to on 22 June 2011 but only partly proclaimed. Part I and sections 7–18, 22, 23, 25(1), 26 and 28 of Part II (the Office of the Information Commissioner) came into operation on 6 January 2012 (Legal Notice 2 of 2012), and section 42(a)–(b) of Part III, on disclosure of personal information by public bodies, followed on 23 August 2021 (Legal Notice 220 of 2021). The rules for the private sector (Part IV) have not been proclaimed.

issues: Planalto source (index 0): after the cache was cleared, a fresh fetch gave NOT-FOUND for 'Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais (LGPD)'. The cause is the page's Windows-1252 encoding with no charset header, which makes fetch-text.py decode the accents as U+FFFD; the quote is not missing. Decoding the raw bytes as cp1252 shows the exact string in the ementa. The page marks the LGPD short title as '(Redação dada pela Lei nº 13.853, de 2019)', so the name was added by the 2019 amendment. The claim that the 1988 Constitution had already created the habeas data writ had no source. The Câmara dos Deputados text of the Constitution's original publication (DOU, 5 October 1988) gives Art. 5 LXXII(a): the writ is granted to ensure knowledge of information about the petitioner held in government or public-character databases. This was added.

The dates are correct: signed 14 August 2018, in force 18 September 2020 per DLA Piper. The RIPD entry was added as independent corroboration. A nuance that is not wrong: the administrative-sanctions articles took effect only on 1 August 2021, and the ANPD provisions earlier, in December 2018.
